about: THE URL-REDACTION PROGRAMS, shared by BOTH redactors: e2e/harness/redact.ts (what the
harness prints) and scripts/ci/redact-artifacts.sh (the bytes CI uploads). One file, so the
two cannot drift apart again - an independent verifier found them matching different
shapes while AGENTS.md said they were the same program (PR #8, R2-FINDING C).
Each pattern has exactly ONE capture group: the part that is KEPT (boundary, scheme,
authority, path). Everything the pattern matches after it - the `?query` and/or
`#fragment` - is replaced. Applied in this order. Valid in JavaScript and Perl alike;
e2e/harness/redaction-corpus.test.ts runs both redactors over the same corpus and checks
every output byte for byte.
FRAGMENTS: `<<NAME>>` in a pattern is replaced by the fragment of that name, which may
itself use fragments declared ABOVE it. Both redactors expand them the same way, once,
before compiling, and an unknown name is an error rather than an empty string. They exist
so the separator spellings (R3-FINDING I: `\u002f`, `\x2F`, `%2F`, `/`, `/`,
`/` for a slash; `\u003f`, `\x3F`, `%3F` for the `?`) are written ONCE.
The alternatives inside a repeated group are kept DISJOINT (`%2F` is a SLASH and never
three PATH characters; `\` never starts a BODY character), because an ambiguous `(a|a)*`
backtracks exponentially on input that does not match. And the HTML-entity slashes come
FIRST in BODY: `&` is also a BODY character, and an alternation tries its branches in order.
A `;` is a BOUNDARY only when it does not end an HTML-entity slash (`/`, `/`,
`/`) - otherwise every entity inside a long path would start a fresh scan to the end
of it, which is quadratic. Fixed-length lookbehinds, because Perl's must be.
`(?!<redacted)` after the separator makes the programs idempotent: a URL an earlier
program already redacted is not matched again by a later one.
Do not edit by hand without re-running that test; do not widen without a corpus case.
